Export a figure at publication resolution and journal column widths

Source: R/mp_export.R
mp_export.Rd

Wraps ggplot2::ggsave() with sensible defaults for journal submission: device inferred from the file extension, millimetre units, 300 dpi, and optional standard column-width presets so figures are sized correctly for single- or double-column layouts.

Usage

mp_export(
  plot,
  filename,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  units = c("mm", "cm", "in"),
  dpi = 300,
  column = c("none", "single", "onehalf", "double"),
  format = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot or patchwork object, or an interactive plotly widget (as returned with interactive = TRUE), which is saved as a self-contained .html page instead.

filename

Output path. For static plots the extension selects the device (.pdf, .png, .tiff, .svg, .eps, .jpg); for an interactive widget it must be .html.

width, height

Dimensions in units. If column is set, width is taken from the preset; if height is NULL it defaults to width * 0.75.

units

One of "mm" (default), "cm" or "in".

dpi

Raster resolution. Common choices: 300 or 600.

column

Column-width preset: "none" (default), "single" (89 mm), "onehalf" (120 mm) or "double" (183 mm).

format

Optional explicit device name overriding the extension.

...

Further arguments passed to ggplot2::ggsave().

Value

The filename, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- mp_ordination(ps, group.by = "Group")
mp_export(p, "figure1.pdf", column = "single")
mp_export(p, "figure1.tiff", column = "double", dpi = 600)
} # }
